tasks.title: Enter the table as GM or player
currentFlow: Open /login, enter the shared table password, and pick the GM or Player role.
The role cookie drives every later authorization decision.

findings.description: Trusted-table role entry works and stays inside the private identity boundary; onboarding must reuse it, not replace it.

tasks.title: Select which player profile this browser acts as
currentFlow: Player picks one of the GM-created profiles; the choice is remembered in localStorage.
Token control, sheet visibility, and inventory requests attach the selected profile ID.

findings.description: Nothing routes a selected profile toward character creation; a profile without linked characters simply sees empty play surfaces.

tasks.title: Create the player profile that will own the new character
currentFlow: GM opens /players, types a display name, and creates the profile.
The profile starts with zero linked characters and no onboarding state.

findings.description: Profile creation is server-authoritative and revision-safe.
There is no concept of an onboarding slot: after creating a profile the GM must remember every remaining manual step in order.

tasks.title: Create the Trainer sheet document
currentFlow: GM opens /sheets, picks a folder, and creates a blank trainer document.
The server allocates a new-trainer-N slug and writes a minimal default runtime sheet.

findings.description: The created document is an empty shell (slug, default name, level) with no creation budgets, no policy, and no ownership.
The blank sheet is immediately a normal library citizen: it can be linked, teamed, and placed in encounters while mechanically empty.
Players cannot create sheets at all; the GM must create the document before a player can even start building.

tasks.title: Enter Trainer identity and presentation
currentFlow: Open the ordinary Trainer editor and fill name, played-by, age, sex, portrait, accent, and narrative blocks field by field.

findings.description: Identity entry is unordered sheet editing; nothing distinguishes required creation fields from optional flavor.

tasks.title: Allocate starting Trainer stat points
currentFlow: Type levelUp values per stat in the stats grid; derived HP and combat values update live.

findings.description: The 10-point creation budget and level-gain budget are table knowledge; the editor accepts any totals.
Overspent or underspent stat totals save silently; nothing blocks play with an illegal allocation.

tasks.title: Choose skill background and resulting skill ranks
currentFlow: Type a free-form background name/description and pick adept/novice/pathetic skills.
Skill ranks derive from background plus Edges, with manual rank bonuses available.

findings.description: Background is free prose; rank floors/caps and adept/novice/pathetic counts are not enforced as a creation decision.

tasks.title: Choose the free Training Feature
currentFlow: Pick one of the four canonical [Training] features in the Trainer editor.

findings.description: Nothing requires the choice at creation; a Trainer can reach play with no Training Feature selected.

tasks.title: Add starting Edges, Features, and classes
currentFlow: Add rows through pickers backed by canonical reference data; automation instances capture identity and choices.
Prerequisites and remaining Edge/Feature counts are displayed but advisory.

findings.description: Creation counts (4 Edges, 4 Features at level 1) live in remainingFeatures/remainingEdges fields the user maintains by hand.
Prerequisite-violating or overspent selections save normally; legality is a display concern, not a gate.

tasks.title: Set starting money, inventory, and equipment
currentFlow: Type the starting money number and add inventory rows by hand or through item pickers.
Equip items through the authoritative equipment workflow after rows exist.

findings.description: Campaign starting money and standard kit are table knowledge; every starter package is retyped per character.
The same standard starting items are re-entered for every new Trainer with no reviewed package to apply.

tasks.title: Create the starter Pokémon sheet document
currentFlow: GM creates a blank pokemon document from the sheet library, then hands the slug to the player or edits it directly.

findings.description: Starter creation begins as an empty document with no species, level, or campaign pool authority.
Which species are legal starters for this campaign exists only in GM memory or prose notes.

tasks.title: Assign species, level, nature, and added stats
currentFlow: Pick the species in the identity panel to pull Pokédex defaults, set level and nature, then type added stat points.

findings.description: The level-based added-stat budget (level + 10) is enforced only as display math; the base/added split relies on user discipline.
Illegal added-stat totals, impossible natures, or non-species forms save without a blocking issue.

tasks.title: Choose starter Abilities and starting Moves
currentFlow: Pick Abilities and level-up Moves through reference-backed pickers on the ordinary sheet.

findings.description: Basic-ability tier rules and the level-up move window are advisory; the picker permits any canonical entry.
A starter can reach play with zero Moves, illegal Abilities, or more than six active Moves.

tasks.title: Confirm capabilities, skills, size, and movement
currentFlow: Species defaults arrive from the Pokédex; users override individual capability and skill cells when needed.

findings.description: Manual overrides can contradict species authority with no record of why; there is no bounded house-rule lane.

tasks.title: Link starters into the Trainer's team
currentFlow: Open the Trainer's Pokémon tab, browse eligible pokemon sheets, and add each starter to currentTeam or boxedPokemon.

findings.description: Team formation is a separate post-creation step the GM or player must remember; nothing connects it to starter creation.
Team slugs are plain strings on the trainer document; renames and deletions can leave dangling or duplicated links.

tasks.title: Link the Trainer and starters to the player profile
currentFlow: GM returns to /players, selects the profile, and links the trainer sheet and each pokemon sheet one by one.

findings.description: Each character is selected twice: once while teaming on the trainer sheet and again while linking on /players.
Forgetting one pokemon link silently removes that starter from player control in live play; nothing checks team/profile consistency.

tasks.title: Review and approve the finished character package
currentFlow: The GM opens each sheet and eyeballs stats, skills, Edges, Features, Moves, and inventory against remembered campaign rules.
Feedback happens out of band; corrections are direct edits to live sheets.

findings.description: There is no submission, snapshot, change-request, or approval record; the GM reviews mutable sheets and edits them directly with no visible history.
Player edits during review change what the GM is looking at; approval is a verbal event with no authority.

tasks.title: See onboarding readiness on the Campaign dashboard
currentFlow: Campaign attention surfaces roster/ownership gaps for existing characters, but has no notion of in-progress character creation.

findings.description: Unstarted or half-built characters are invisible as campaign work; the GM tracks onboarding progress outside the app.

tasks.title: Bring the new party into an encounter
currentFlow: GM builds an encounter and adds the new Trainer and each starter as cast/reserves by picking sheets individually.

findings.description: The Builder has no grouped Trainer+team candidate; each member is re-picked and re-sided by hand.
Blank or half-built sheets are indistinguishable from ready characters when adding encounter participants.

tasks.title: Perform the first legal action with the new character
currentFlow: Player opens the encounter; token control derives from profile-linked sheets; declares a Move or other action.

findings.description: First-action success depends on every earlier manual step (links, team, moves, stats) having been done correctly; failures surface here as inexplicable missing control or empty action lists.

tasks.title: Adopt an existing character into the campaign
currentFlow: Existing or imported sheets are linked to a profile manually; validity against campaign rules is judged by eye.
Structural repairs happen by editing the sheet or importing corrected JSON.

findings.description: Fixing malformed legacy sheets means editing JSON exports or the live document by hand; there is no bounded, previewed repair workflow.
Adoption never validates the character against campaign policy, ownership conflicts, or dangling team references.
